categories.main_business_segments: Matsui Construction Co., Ltd. operates two main business segments: the Construction Business, which includes general contracting for building and civil engineering projects, and the Real Estate Business, which involves the sale and leasing of land and buildings, as well as design and supervision services for construction projects. The group also participates in PFI (Private Finance Initiative) projects through an affiliated company.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages both traditional and modern construction technologies, with a particular emphasis on the preservation and integration of historic shrine and temple construction techniques. It utilizes project-based cost management, BIM (Building Information Modeling), and promotes environmentally conscious construction methods such as ZEB (Zero Energy Building) and ZEH (Zero Energy House). The company also employs DX (digital transformation) tools and advanced project management systems.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Matsui Construction serves a diverse customer base, including public sector clients (local governments and public institutions) and private sector clients (corporations, religious organizations, and individuals). Its end markets include public facilities, educational institutions, religious and cultural heritage sites, commercial buildings, and residential developments.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s operations are concentrated in Japan, with headquarters in Tokyo and regional branches in Osaka, Nagoya, Tohoku, Hokuriku, and Kyushu. All reported sales and assets are domestic, with no significant overseas operations.
categories.supply_chain_position: Matsui Construction operates as a downstream player in the construction supply chain, acting as a general contractor that manages project delivery, coordinates subcontractors, and interfaces directly with end clients. It also engages in downstream real estate activities such as property sales and leasing.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include qualitative growth over scale expansion, strengthening the business foundation, and enhancing corporate quality and responsibility. The company is focused on digital transformation (DX), environmental sustainability (carbon neutrality, ZEB/ZEH adoption), and the preservation and advancement of traditional construction techniques. There is also an emphasis on workforce diversity, next-generation management development, and resilience to climate and disaster risks. No significant proprietary R&D activities are reported.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through construction contract work, recognized based on project progress (percentage-of-completion method), as well as through the sale and leasing of real estate properties and provision of design and supervision services. Rental income from owned properties and dividends from investment securities also contribute to revenue.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Matsui Construction is a mid-sized general contractor in Japan, positioned below the major 'super general contractors' but with a strong reputation in traditional and cultural construction projects. Its competitors include other mid-tier and regional construction firms, as well as larger national players. The company differentiates itself through its expertise in shrine, temple, and cultural heritage construction.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated net sales were ¥99.3 billion, with operating profit of ¥3.38 billion and net profit attributable to shareholders of ¥2.73 billion. The company has shown moderate sales growth (2.4% year-on-year), a significant recovery in profitability, and maintains a strong equity ratio (62.6%). The workforce numbers around 762 employees. The company targets further qualitative growth and stable profitability under its mid-term plan.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Matsui Construction emphasizes its long-standing tradition (founded in 1586), technical expertise in both modern and traditional construction (especially shrines, temples, and cultural assets), and commitment to quality, safety, and environmental sustainability. The company positions itself as a reliable, community-oriented builder with a strong financial base and a focus on customer satisfaction and social contribution.
